newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed up from the New York close on overseas buying, gold dealers and traders said on Tuesday.
The gold market saw two-way business from traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), industry sources said.

"Basically they're not too impressed with the dollar/yen and if they expected the dollar/yen to come off lower, then it's normal to sell the metal in yen terms," one gold trader at an international bank said.
Any selling interest from Japan was absorbed by professional buying, gold traders said.
Other Hong Kong dealers said the Japanese were buying gold to square their books and on shortcovering.
Bullion ended at US$379.00/379.50 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$378.60/379.00 close on Monday.
The dollar was trading at about 113.75 yen at 4.21 pm (0821 GMT).
When Europe entered the market in afternoon trade, further buying emerged on shortcovering, gold dealers said.
But gold would remain range-bound between $378.50 and $379.50 per ounce, dealers said.
If support did not hold at the critical $377 per ounce, then gold would slide to $375, gold traders said, noting that the market remained uncertain on direction.
Tight short-term gold borrowing rates provided an opportunity for arbitrage traders who were buying loco London and selling local tael gold, some gold dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,494 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.00 from its previous fix at -7.00.
